title: High-day counts left three-day ozone episodes unresolved in four selected US bird-survey samples in 2005-2019
abstract: We tested whether high-day counts fix the presence of three-day ozone episodes before selected US bird surveys. Exact bounds used 1,120 complete 30-day windows in two regions and two periods in 2005-2019. At a cutoff above 70 ppb, counts left 146 windows unresolved. The fractions were 4.2-20.8% across four samples. Keeping the adjacent high-high pair count reduced the set to 33 windows, or 0.4-6.3%. Of 74 observed positive windows, 70 could become negative under a permutation with the same full concentration distribution. Complete dates, monitor alternatives and duplicate checks did not remove all count ambiguity. The bounds need no random-order model. They are not fitted error rates or estimates of bird harm. Selected roadside surveys, shared monitors, overlapping windows and complete-record selection limit wider use. No climate interaction or biological response is tested. Code, aggregate results, source hashes and an external-input retrieval script permit reproduction.

display.caption: Exact episode-label ambiguity after daily order is removed. Blue retains the high-day count. Orange also retains the adjacent high-high pair count. Fractions describe selected complete windows, without population uncertainty intervals.
